strategies.text:
Overview

Mega Starmie is a hilariously looking new Mega with alleged access to the powerful, unreleased, Liquidation+ move. Mega Starmie's move pool is heavily diverse with access to typical water moves alongside psychic and rock type moves (power gem)

This guide is centered on maximizing Necrozma Dawn Wings' energy gain and spamming Moongeist Beam.

Est Time to Win: 260.0s-290.0s

Main Strategy

Mega Raichu Y pushes very high DPS at the cost of survivability. It's important to dodge heavy charge hitting moves on Raichu Y while allowing Necrozma Dawn Wings to sponge hits directly.

No real advanced mechanics beyond swapping are required here. None of Mega Starmie's move pool pose a great threat to Necrozma Dawn Wings.

Something to note is Necrozma Dawn Wings can only sponge up to 1 Hydro-pump freely before needing to actively swap or dodge the next one.


Advanced Strategy:

If engaging in TPC, Tick Perfect Cast, Psycho Cut is the preferred fast move of choice. This redistributes damage from Shadow Claw into Moongeist beam by increasing EPS at the cost of fast move DPS. The trade off is generally positive toward Moongeist Beam.

strategies.text:
Overview

This route uses Mega Raichu Y and Regieleki while absorbing non-lethal moves. Recommended to dodge Hydropumps.

Est Time to Win 285.0s-295.0s


Main Strategy

Due to the lineup's low defense and low hp it is crucial to manage each attacker's bulk. Each pokemon can comfortably tank 1 charge move (other than hydro-pump) with some room to tank fast moves. Catch Tanking and Hot-Swapping are critical for juggling energy appropriately.


The main carry is Mega Raichu Y, expect to get out 2-3 Zap Cannon+ (lvl 4).

Secondary carries are Regieleki's able to pump out 1-2 Thunder Cages depending on if they absorb a charge move or not.


Aim to TPC both of these moves as best you can (not necessarily required and most importantly do not "drop" any charge moves from fainting. Losing a thunder cage or Zap Cannon+ (lvl 4) can greatly hinder your DPS.


Teaching wild charge on Raichu Y can help with closing the raid in tight situations.

strategies.strategyName: Hot Swapping Your Way to Victory
strategies.text:
Overview

Mega Starmie is a pretty straightforward solo, especially if using the current premier and bane of Psychic and Ghost types, Dawn Wings Necrozma — which is ironically, a Ghost/Psychic type. With the advent of Mega Raichu Y's Plus move, you can do it without needing a full Ghost team. Additionally, Mega Sceptile in Sunny weather will also work.

Estimated Time: 290-300 seconds

Main Strategy

Mega Starmie does not have a lot of moves that will deal massive damage, at least not enough to reliably catch tank. Even Hydro Pump will raise about slightly less than 50% energy in a neutral setting. In this scenario, hot swapping is probably the best way to go.

The biggest question for Mega Starmie is: Psycho Cut or Shadow Claw? The former generates energy better, the latter provides more consistent damage. For the solo scenario I faced, I encountered Water Gun/Psywave, and used a combination of Shadow Claw and Psycho Cut due to item limitations. I think this is possibly the best mix; use Shadow Claw for your first few Dawn Wings to frontload damage, and Psycho Cut for the last couple to quickly generate energy with the clock ticking down.

My settings allowed for a no-relobby win, however other VODs demonstrate that even with rejoins, you can push for better times. Speed or survivability? That's a choice only you can decide, with your own scenario.
